title: Program: Pluggable Cognitive Memory Providers for TraceDecay V2
description:
Build a commercially viable TraceDecay V2 derivative for coding agents that can use multiple memory
systems without coupling their internal representation to TraceDecay's native fact store. The first
providers are TraceDecay Native and NCM; OCEAN is a deliberately deferred provider until its versioned
specification exists.

The program remains a single Rust monorepo and preserves Zackary Jackson's upstream architecture wherever
possible. Product-owned crates, contracts, adapters, tests, and integration mounts must be easy to identify,
remove, compare, and rebase across future upstream V2 checkpoints.
design:
Treat TraceDecay as the host and coding-context authority. Add a capability-based provider boundary above
concrete memory implementations. Keep the existing native store authoritative for explicit durable facts;
cognitive providers return advisory recall candidates and receive observations/outcomes through an
idempotent dispatch layer. A shared context compiler validates scope and provenance before provider output
reaches an agent.

Delivery is staged: pin/reproduce upstream, define contracts, create isolated crates, prove Native parity,
add dispatch and recall seams, integrate NCM first as an observer, then enable guarded active mode only after
conformance and evaluation gates pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The branch remains traceable to the exact upstream PR #707 floor and has a repeatable convergence process.
- [ ] TraceDecay Native works through the provider boundary with no observable regression or forced migration.
- [ ] NCM passes provider conformance and can run in observer mode without influencing the agent.
- [ ] Guarded active NCM mode passes the stale-memory, crash-recovery, scope-isolation, and provider-failure journeys.
- [ ] OCEAN has a reserved provider slot but no speculative implementation is counted as delivered.
- [ ] All program work is represented in versioned .beads/issues.jsonl and governed by inherited agent context.

comments.text:
REOPENED by root after adversarial closure audit (wf_ebb9eac2-40f).

My closure comment claimed: 'synchronous SQLite work runs under tokio::task::spawn_blocking instead of on a runtime worker.' That claim is false as written, and I am retracting it.

Two synchronous SQLite paths still run directly on a tokio runtime worker:

1. observation_journey.rs:1766 — SqliteObservationJournal::open performs WAL creation, synchronous=FULL pragmas, the DDL batch, and an unbounded 'SELECT ... FROM tdmem_observation_withheld_v2' full-table revalidation (sqlite/schema.rs:295 -> sqlite/row.rs:167-181), all inside one IMMEDIATE transaction committed with fsync. It is reached from mount_and_replay (:1911), which project_composition.rs:1097 awaits during project open. So project open blocks a runtime worker on fsync'd disk I/O whose cost grows without bound with the withheld audit table.

2. observation_journey.rs:1522 — DeliveryRuntimeV1::shutdown (write transaction + 256-row reap + inspect, runtime/delivery.rs:374-393) runs on the async task, thirteen lines below the spawn_blocking the same function already uses for the worker join. It can park a worker behind the delivery thread's in-flight fsync'd transaction on the same Mutex<Connection>.

Required to re-close:
- Hoist SqliteObservationJournal::open into mount_and_replay under spawn_blocking and pass the opened journal into mount_project_observation_journey.
- Bound validate_withheld_rows (sqlite/row.rs:167) with LIMIT + resume so open cost is bounded.
- Wrap runtime.shutdown in spawn_blocking inside the existing timeout_at(deadline, ...), matching :1509.

AC1-AC4 (causal binding to the canonical log, crash-loss freedom, watermark-driven replay, single-writer discipline) were probed independently and were NOT refuted. Only the blocking-I/O claim fails.

description:
Make recalled experience accountable to task outcomes. Useful experience should strengthen, harmful or stale

- [ ] Candidate lessons cannot become canonical rules without an audited promotion path.

- [ ] Provider-specific internal learning remains private to the provider while shared lifecycle events stay portable.

comments.author: satan
comments.text:
REOPENED by root after adversarial closure audit (wf_ebb9eac2-40f).

My closure comment claimed: 'vacuous zero-admission checks score Indeterminate (0 bp).' That claim does not hold outside the scope/corruption family, and I am retracting it.

Defect A — evaluate_check('exact_source_target') (baseline.rs:3204-3212) returns Pass, weight 0.2 = 2000 bp, for ANY terminal except InvalidRequest. The Native lane reaches it through delete_by_source (:2435), which reads back the host-preflight refusal record that dispatch_with_reply pushed with terminal_code=capability_unsupported, provider_contacted=false, diagnostic=host.capability_undeclared (:2617-2640). So the Native lane earns 2000 bp for a deletion that was never dispatched and deleted nothing — precisely the vacuity the closure claims is scored Indeterminate. verified_absence and restart_persistence already handle this correctly at :3116-3121; exact_source_target does not.

Defect B — commit_item (baseline.rs:2169) pushes onto batch.committed unconditionally, ignoring outcome. For the Native lane every observe returns capability_unsupported with committed_effect_state='none', so effect_boundary (:2980, 3000 bp) reports items as committed that the provider explicitly refused.

Required to re-close:
- Treat CapabilityUnsupported | Cancelled | DeadlineExceeded | ProviderUnavailable as Indeterminate for exact_source_target, matching :3116-3121.
- Push onto batch.committed only on a committing terminal, and score effect_boundary Indeterminate when no item committed.
- Re-run the baseline reports; the Native lane's privacy_deletion and effect_boundary scores change.

Also recorded, not blocking this bead: the Native lane is a capability-floor lane, not a third measured baseline. observation_kind (baseline.rs:3239-3256) emits only three kinds and parse_observation (provider-native/src/lib.rs:365-367) rejects everything but native.fact_promoted.v1, so the Native store is empty in every scenario and its cost row is byte-identical to no-memory. tdmem-0905 would otherwise compare NCM against two identical zero lanes. This must be stated explicitly in the baseline report rather than presented as a third measured lane.

title: Post-#707 convergence invariants not literally satisfied (lsp shutdown deadline, same-checkout test bin)
description:
Found by the Sol product-loss reviewer while landing upstream PR #707 (5749e4fc) into the product branch. Neither is a merge regression (both behaviours predate the merge), but each convergence-map entry states an invariant the code does not literally satisfy. Either make the code satisfy the invariant or correct the invariant wording; never silently drop it.

1. crates/tracedecay-daemon-service/src/invocation/lsp.rs — entry invariant: LSP shutdown consumes only the remaining shared deadline and never creates a fresh timeout. Code: expire_all_until(deadline) first awaits lsp_lease_tasks.shutdown() without the caller's deadline, so that await is unbounded relative to the shared deadline. Fix: bound that await with the same deadline (tokio::time::timeout_at) and test it.

2. crates/tracedecay/tests/common/mod.rs — entry invariant: integration tests run a same-checkout CLI. Code: tracedecay_bin() accepts any explicit TRACEDECAY_TEST_BIN whose --version has the same release prefix, so a binary from another worktree passes. Fix: verify the binary's build identity (git sha embedded via TRACEDECAY_GIT_SHA) matches this checkout, or restrict the override to paths under this checkout's target dir; test both the accept and reject paths.

Minor, same review: project_composition.rs project_recall_routing_policy rejects every Some(fallback) configuration while the rustdoc and the entry say fallback is forbidden "unless the routing gate pins a complete rule". Align wording with behaviour (only one provider is registered, so no pinned fallback can ever be valid) or implement the pinned rule.
close_reason: done

title: Crash and restart fuzzing between host commit and provider acknowledgement
description:
Kill the process at randomized points between host commit and provider acknowledgement and
prove nothing is lost, nothing is applied twice, and the watermark resumes correctly.

## Method
- A fuzz driver that runs the mounted journey, injects a kill (abort, SIGKILL of a child, or a
  panic at an instrumented point) at a seeded random position across: after canonical commit
  before journal write; after journal write before dispatch; after dispatch before reply;
  after reply before receipt persist; after receipt before watermark advance.
- Restart, replay from the durable watermark, and assert: every committed canonical observation
  is present in the journal exactly once; every provider effect is either applied exactly once or
  reported `unknown` with a reconciliation receipt (never silently absent, never doubled); the
  watermark equals the last durably acknowledged sequence.
- Run N seeds (hundreds) in CI-affordable time; record the seed on any failure so it reproduces.

## Done when
- The driver exists and runs against the real mounted path.
- Either N seeds pass clean, or the defects found are fixed and their seeds are added as
  permanent regression cases.
- The catch-all `Err(error)` branch in the live replay loop (`observation_journey.rs:~1446`) that
  treats permanent admission refusals as transient — stream stalls forever, no halt recorded,
  identical warn every 5s — is fixed: non-transient errors go through record_halt/clear_halt.
Drives what tdmem-0506 and tdmem-0508 were asking for.

title: Make Native ingest session observations instead of refusing them
description:
Native must actually store session observations. Today it refuses all of them.

## Root cause
`crates/tracedecay-memory-provider-native/src/lib.rs` `parse_observation` accepts only
`native.fact_promoted.v1`. Every `session.message_committed.v1` the mounted journey dispatches
is answered `capability_unsupported` with diagnostic `native.observation_staged`, and
`observation_journey.rs` settles the row `Rejected` after one attempt. This is stated in the
module's own doc comment ("what is not yet true is that Native ingests session messages").

Consequence: the store is empty in every scenario, recall has nothing to return, and every
downstream bead (recall bridge, host hooks, learning, evaluation) is unprovable.

## Done when
- Native ingests `session.message_committed.v1` (and whichever other kinds the journey emits) into
  a real persisted representation in the Native store, under the exact coding scope.
- A mounted journey test asserts a delivery settles `acknowledged` with `receipts: 1`, not
  `rejected`. Today every journey test asserts `("rejected", 1)`; at least one must flip.
- A subsequent recall through the mounted cognitive-recall route returns a candidate derived from
  that observation, with provenance pointing back to it.
- Idempotency: the same observation dispatched twice settles `duplicate`, not a second row.
- No provider-name branching outside registry/adapters; output stays advisory.
close_reason: Delivered in 44f4fbc17: Native stages session.message_committed.v1 into the product-owned staged store under the provider-state directory (durable commit before Success, duplicate returns stored evidence, conflict on divergence, tombstoned eviction, secondary source-identity uniqueness) and recalls staged rows as advisory exact_coding_scope candidates merged with canonical facts under one budget. Mounted journey test flipped from (rejected,1) to (acknowledged,1). Root-verified: workspace check, default check, focused tests, gates. Cross-session recall tracked in tdmem-b8q.

title: Adversarial provider harness against the mounted dispatch and recall paths
description:
An adversarial `MemoryProvider` implementation and a test suite that drives the mounted dispatch
and recall paths through it. This is the harness that finds real bugs; build it as product-owned
code under `crates/tracedecay-memory-conformance` (or a sibling crate), mounted against the real
`observation_journey` and `cognitive_recall` routes in the root crate.

## Behaviours the provider must be able to exhibit, selectable per call
- Crash mid-dispatch (panic / process abort after receiving the call, before replying)
- Hang past the deadline (never reply; assert the host's `DeadlineExceeded` fires and the worker
  is not parked forever)
- Protocol violation: wrong terminal for the operation, payload on a non-success terminal,
  reply for a different `operation_id`, `state_generation` going backwards
- Oversized reply beyond `ProviderLimits`
- Duplicate acknowledgement naming another mutation
- Cancellation ignored (keeps working after the token fires)
- Success with corrupted effect evidence (digest mismatch)

## Done when
- Each behaviour has a test against the MOUNTED path (not just the fabric), asserting the typed
  terminal the host produces, that the journal row settles correctly, that no worker thread is
  leaked (assert thread/task counts before and after), and that the daemon stays responsive.
- At least one real defect found and fixed, or an explicit statement that none was found with
  the list of behaviours exercised.
Drives what tdmem-1107 and tdmem-1009 were asking for.
close_reason: Accepted after Fable 5.1 final review and independent root validation. The mounted adversarial dispatch/recall suite exercises crash, hang/deadline, cancellation-ignore, protocol-terminal/payload/operation-id/generation violations, oversized replies, duplicate acknowledgement, corrupted effect evidence, exact worker census, and daemon responsiveness. Real defects fixed: cancellation is now monotonic at every pre-contact, delivery, and settle edge; worker-start rollback and stranded-worker accounting settle exactly once; fixed-sleep/yield synchronization was replaced with deadline-bounded transition waits. Provider-registry, conformance, cognitive-recall, project-composition, and core mounted observation suites passed; the only later compile interruption is an unrelated tdmem-1001 file being actively edited. Convergence invariants were recorded and dependency-direction plus ownership gates pass.

title: Volume and backpressure soak through the journal and dispatcher
description:
Push volume through the journal and dispatcher and measure what breaks.

## Scenarios
- 10k+ observations committed faster than the provider acknowledges: assert queue stays within
  its declared bound, no observation is silently dropped (every one is either acknowledged,
  rejected with a typed terminal, or still queued and visible), and backpressure is reported
  rather than absorbed.
- Sustained run: disk growth of the journal, the withheld audit table, and the Native store over
  time; retention sweep actually reclaims.
- The audit-found unbounded scan: `validate_withheld_rows` (`sqlite/row.rs:167`) runs a full-table
  read inside `SqliteObservationJournal::open`. Grow the withheld table large and measure project
  open latency; bound it with LIMIT + resume and prove open cost is now flat.
- Provider slow but alive (replies at 90% of deadline): throughput, worker occupancy, no runaway
  memory.

## Done when
- A runnable soak (cargo test with an env-gated size, or a bin) with measured numbers recorded
  in the bead comment: peak queue depth, drop count (must be 0), open latency before/after
  bounding, disk growth per 1k observations.
- The two blocking-I/O defects on tdmem-0502 are fixed as part of this: journal open under
  spawn_blocking, DeliveryRuntimeV1::shutdown under spawn_blocking.
Drives what tdmem-0505 and the reopened tdmem-0502 were asking for.

title: Harden the repaired product gates against the 12 demonstrated bypasses
description:
Four product gates were repaired on 2026-09-02 (workflow wf_26453d27-d61). Three of the four
went green but an adversarial anti-weakening reviewer demonstrated concrete, reproduced bypasses
in the repaired gates. These are gate-ROBUSTNESS holes: a future change could pass the gate while
violating the invariant. No live violation is known today.

Do not treat these gates as trustworthy until this bead closes.

## check-memory-composition-feature.py (7 demonstrated bypasses)

1. `strip_cfg_test_modules` strips any module whose cfg text merely CONTAINS the token `test`.
   A production module under `#[cfg(not(test))]` is therefore erased from every production scan.
   Fix: parse the cfg predicate semantically; strip only when the predicate implies test is true.
   Fail closed on negation, `any(test, feature=...)`, nested all/any, and unknown predicates.
2. The transitive feature-closure proof treats every `package/feature` edge as an opaque string
   and checks only exact `package` / `dep:package` membership. Adding
   `tracedecay-memory-hygiene/hotpath` to `production` activates the optional support dependency
   with zero gate errors. Fix: normalize local-feature, `dep:package`, strong `package/feature`
   and weak `package?/feature` forms; treat every strong support-package feature edge as
   activating that dependency.
3. Default activation and routing checks search raw whole-file text. Setting the real config
   default to `true` while leaving the `false` fragment in a block comment passes. So does
   removing/renaming the real routing struct while preserving its fragment. Fix: use a code mask
   and structurally scoped item bodies; require exactly one executable field initialization.
4. `gated_allowlist` accepts a module as feature-gated when the declaration occurs anywhere in
   raw source. Removing the real `#[cfg(feature = "memory-provider-host")]` and appending the old
   declaration inside a block comment passes. Fix: locate the actual module item in the code mask
   and prove its associated cfg predicate.
5. The dormant-mount proof does not prove activation is examined BEFORE work begins. Inserting
   `start_background_worker();` at the top of `mount_project_memory_provider_host` passes. Fix:
   require the activation match to dominate all side effects, or the Disabled branch to return
   before any side-effect-capable call.
6. The two consumer checks require guarded-call fragments to EXIST but do not require ALL calls
   to be inside those guards. Adding an unconditional `mount_and_replay().await?` before the
   preserved `if ...registry().is_some()` block passes. Fix: enumerate all production call sites
   and require the expected count, not fragment presence.
7. Provider-name branching is detected only when the comparison statement itself contains a
   recognized identity-like token. `let expected = ...::NATIVE_PROVIDER_ID; candidate == expected`
   passes. Fix: dataflow-aware inspection, or forbid provider identity constants outside the
   registry/adapter boundary.

## check-memory-dependency-direction.py (3 demonstrated bypasses)

1. `extract_crate_paths` recognizes only literal `<crate_root>::...` spellings, so whole-crate
   aliases defeat it: `use tokio as runtime; runtime::spawn(...)`,
   `use std::thread as workers; workers::spawn(...)`, and
   `use tracedecay_application as app; app::now_micros()` each produced zero errors.
   Fix: fail closed on whole-crate/module aliases and `extern crate ... as ...` for every
   contracted root and every forbidden capability root; track re-exports transitively.
2. Executor access is pinned by `file.rs::function` NAME only — not a unique function identity,
   call expression, or occurrence count. A second `tokio::spawn` inside the already-approved
   `bridge_cancellation`, and a distinct same-named method, both pass.
   Fix: pin resolved call expressions with fully qualified identity and exact occurrence counts.
3. `allowed_dependency_features` compares only explicitly requested `features`; default features
   are rejected only for dependencies separately named in `dependencies_requiring_default_features_off`.
   Fix: require `default-features = false` for every dependency claiming an exact reviewed
   feature set, or model the resolved default closure.

## check-coding-memory-authority-matrix-core.py (2 demonstrated bypasses)

1. `rust_doc_blocks()` skips all attribute lines including `#[cfg(...)]`, so the required
   authority sentence can be attached to a `#[cfg(any())]` accessor that never compiles while the
   live accessor documents distributed authority. Verified: gate exits 0.
   Fix: preserve and evaluate intervening attributes; fail closed if the asserted accessor carries
   any cfg/cfg_attr.
2. `doc_assertion_holds()` uses `item.startswith(prefix)` with prefix `pub fn configuration_target`,
   so attaching the sentence to `configuration_target_legacy` passes. Verified: gate exits 0.
   Fix: match the parsed function name exactly, or require the boundary `pub fn configuration_target(`.

## Settled, no action

check-upstream-vendor-floor.py is NOT a real failure. Bare invocation on the product branch is
refused BY DESIGN: it is a preflight meant to run with --source-ref from a
`sync/upstream/<candidate-short-sha>` branch, per product/upstream/README.md and the
`sync/upstream/**` trigger in .github/workflows/product-upstream.yml. Its 19-test contract suite
passes, including the test locking down this exact refusal. Reviewer verdict: sound.
close_reason: Descoped: hardening product gates for a system that is not yet working.
